newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - 31 July.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - 31 July.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- NORTERN IRELAND COULD GET BEEF BAN EXEMPTION

Agriculture minister Jack Cunningham revealed plans to urge the European Commission to lift the ban in Northern Ireland of the export of beef from herds certified free of BSE in a move to crumble the nationwide ban on beef exports. Mr Cunningham has announced his intentions even at the risk of angering cabinet colleagues representing Wales and Scotland but believes the breakthrough, which could lift bans on Northern Irish meat within a year, would be significant.
-- DEFENCE PROCUREMENT REVIEW AIMS TO SAVE 900M STG A YEAR

Defence secretary George Robertson promised a review of the nine billion stg defence budget offering a 900 million stg saving by utilising modern procurement techniques and ensuring the timely conclusion of projects. Mr Robertson commented that delays and cost overruns could be eliminated to still provide strong armed forces, but not at any price.
-- LIQUIDATOR FAILS TO SUE BANK OVER BCCI LICENCE

Deloitte & Touche, the firm responsible for the liquidation of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International since its collapse in 1991, lost its case at the High Court to sue the Bank of England for misconduct for issuing BCCI with a banking licence in 1980. The judge ruled that the Bank of England had not acted dishonestly by granting a licence to the fraudulent BCCI and so the appeal for 800 million stg for its 6,000 UK depositors was not given.
-- BECKETT STANDS FIRM ON REGIONAL POLICY

Trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett has affirmed her position over regional affairs against the deputy prime minister John Prescott, the man in control of environment, transport and local government, by publishing figures that identifies the disparities in the national economical spread. The report shows the Southeast far more financially secure than the rest of the nation and gives support for Mrs Beckett to retain the traditional contol over regional trade and foreign investment.
-- COUNTRY LIFE LURES CITY MONEY

The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors revealed that the demand for rural retreats has sustained the price of farmland in the year's second quarter, despite a slump in the farming industry, with average sale values only down two per cent from last year at 7,127 stg per hectare. The surprising figures do not reflect the weak beef, cereal and milk prices caused by the strength of the green pound, the Ecu-based aid payments artificial exchange rate.
-- MCI UNDERLINES AMBITION FOR US LOCAL CALLS

The chief financial officer of MCI Communications Corp (MCIC.O) Douglas Maine has announced the company's firm intention to penetrate the US local telephone market following the recent warning of a $800m loss in doing so. The company earlier agreed to a $24 billion takeover by British Telecommunications but contention over the local call losses has urged BT to seek a renegotiation of the deal.
-- MISYS TO SELL INSURANCE OVER INTERNET

Leading supplier of insurance broker software systems Misys is to sell a range of 30 car insurance policies to the public bringing the company into competition with its customers who buy its quote-tracking databases. The "Screen Trade" service is due to be launched in September but has received criticism from analysts that the quotes used from only eight insurance companies is too small to compete effectively with the 180 insurers on the brokers databases.
-- ENERGY GROUP SHARE PRICE SUGGESTS REFERRAL

Investors inability to close the gap on the 690p per share offer by PacifiCorp for the recently demergered Hanson division Energy Group has led industry analysts to suggest that trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett will refer the deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission by next Tuesday. The PacifiCorp group is bidding to take control of a further 61.6 per cent of the energy company but Energy Group shares closed down 2.5p at 656p yesterday indicating a lack of confidence from investors.
-- GRANTCHESTER IN 35M STG RETAIL DEAL

Retail warehouse investor Grantchester has announced an agreed 35 million stg purchase of 260,000 square feet of retail wharehouses in south Wales, Scotland, Falkirk and Devon in preparation for an expected out-of-town retail boom that will give one-third of all retail to this sector by 2000. The company now has 22 out-of-town sites providing an aggregate annual income of more than 17.5 million stg.
